newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Profit-taking halts S.Africa shares' recent run-up.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking halts S.Africa shares' recent run-up.

text.p: South African shares' run-up of the past two days was halted on Wednesday with stocks toppling off their high levels on profit-taking and as futures baskets were unwound.
Dealers said share prices had been inflated since the futures close-out on Monday and the market needed a period of consolidation.

Industrial shares slid further towards the close of the trading day as Wall Street began Wednesday's session softer. The industrial index lost 56.5 points to 8,155.2 dragging down the the overall index 36 points to 6,911.1.
Gold shares took a knock, uninspired by bullion's hold on the $383 level, dealers said. The gold index ended 20.2 points or over one percent weaker at 1,756.3.
But dealers said despite the dip on Wednesday, overall market sentiment remained positive.
